record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: Which experimentally accessible observables can provide a direct and robust signature of multinucleon, or 2p2h, neutrino interactions even after strong final-state interactions distort the primary hadronic distributions, so that competing models of quasielastic-like events can be discriminated reliably?

evidence.quote: Ultimately, it would be important to find a more direct experimental signature for the multinucleon processes.
However, the primary distributions will be heavily distorted by FSI and, therefore, model discrimination would require a high precision and a considerable improvements in the Monte Carlo simulations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In neutrino–nucleus scattering at intermediate energies (roughly 0.1–10 GeV), "quasielastic-like" charged-current events on a nuclear target include genuine one-body quasielastic interactions as well as two-particle–two-hole (2p2h) multinucleon excitations, in which the incoming neutrino couples to a correlated pair of nucleons (through meson-exchange currents and/or short-range correlations) producing two outgoing nucleons. The primary hadronic final state of a 2p2h process is, however, strongly modified by final-state interactions (FSI) as the ejected nucleons propagate through the residual nucleus, so that the kinematic distributions actually observed in a detector are no longer those of the primary vertex.

Identify a set of experimentally accessible observables — constructed from the measurable charged lepton kinematics and/or the kinematics and multiplicities of outgoing hadrons (protons, neutrons, pions) detected after FSI — that constitutes a direct and robust signature of the 2p2h component of the cross section. The observables must be such that, after realistic FSI distortion of the primary distributions on common nuclear targets (carbon, oxygen, argon), competing theoretical models of quasielastic-like neutrino–nucleus interactions (different 1p1h spectral functions, RPA corrections, and 2p2h/MEC models) can be discriminated reliably from data.
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains an active research topic. Recent theoretical work (e.g., on exclusive hadron observables from the Valencia 2p2h model, 2024–2025) and experimental analyses by T2K, MINERvA, MicroBooNE and NOvA continue to propose and test candidate observables (transverse kinematic imbalance, proton multiplicities, lepton-hadron correlations) but no single observable has been established as a definitive, FSI-robust signature; the experimental picture across MiniBooNE/MINERvA/T2K remains inconsistent.

status_evidence.title: Exclusive Hadron Observables in Neutrino Induced 2p2h Multinucleon Knockout
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work explores combined lepton and hadron kinematic observables from the exclusive Valencia 2p2h model... compared with democratically distributed outgoing nucleon kinematics as currently treated in neutrino event generators.
status_evidence.claim: Identification of FSI-robust 2p2h observables is still being actively proposed and studied.

status_evidence.title: Sensitivity of Neutrino-Nucleus Interaction Measurements to 2p2h Excitations
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical models differ substantially in their predicted 2p2h strengths, and the experimental picture of 2p2h interactions obtained from MiniBooNE, MINERvA, and T2K measurements is confused.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus signature exists; experimental discrimination remains unresolved.
